correctness.rationale: Ma Theorem 2.3 order-three decomposition gives exact signed rank-one coefficients. For alpha in (-1,0), one negative vector v2 is uniformly absorbed with a2||R^-1/2 v2||^2<1/8 from r_n>=1/(n+2), D(n)>=(n+3)^3, and elementary zeta tail. The other negative rank-one term forces a negative vector since sum |v0|^2/r diverges logarithmically and positive cross sum with v1 converges. Dense operator range carries negative inertia to compact selfcommutator. Proof establishes exact multiplicity one in entire claimed interval.

value.rationale: At order three, unlike orders one and two, the exact defect has two independent negative-coefficient rank-one terms, so qualitative nonhyponormality allows either one or two negative eigenvalues. The result gives a complete natural exact signed-spectral invariant throughout -1<alpha<0 and a uniform nontrivial absorption argument relevant to higher orders.
